records.source: Τότε προσέρχονται τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσιν τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων;
records.gloss: Then come to the Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes saying, \v 2 Because of what the disciples of you break the tradition of the elders?
pieces: Then Pharisees and scribes arrived from Jerusalem and put a question to Jesus:
"Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples go against the tradition handed down by the elders?

L.1: Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem come to Jesus, saying,
L.2: "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples break the tradition of the elders?

R.1: Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came from Jerusalem to see Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
R.2: "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers break the rules that our leaders of long ago handed down?

decisions.choice: the tradition of the elders: teaching handed down by earlier teachers alongside the written law
decisions.reason: The Pharisees kept rules passed on from teacher to student that applied the law to daily life. Mark 7:3-4 describes some of them. They were not part of the written law.

decisions.choice: from Jerusalem: from the center of Jewish leadership
decisions.reason: These questioners have come a long way from the city of the temple and the high council. Their coming shows that Jesus's work is now watched from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: break: step over, fail to keep
decisions.reason: The verb means to go beyond a line. The same verb is used in Jesus's reply (15:3).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: go against (B), break (R), the same word at 15:2 and 15:3
alternatives: different words in the two verses
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with the verb of their own question. Each level keeps one word for both verses so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law; our leaders of long ago
decisions.reason: Readable says who the scribes were and that the elders here are teachers of earlier generations, not the town elders of the day.

records.heading: The elders' tradition and God's command

records.source: οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.
records.gloss: Not for they wash the hands of them when bread they eat.
pieces: They eat their meals without first washing their hands."

L.2: For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."

R.2: They do not wash their hands in the special way before they eat."

decisions.choice: wash their hands: a washing for religious purity, not for cleanliness
decisions.reason: The law required priests to wash their hands before serving (Exodus 30:19-21). The tradition extended a ritual washing to ordinary meals (Mark 7:3). Not doing it was a matter of purity, not hygiene.

decisions.choice: eat bread: eat a meal
decisions.reason: To eat bread is a common way of saying to have a meal.

decisions.choice: in the special way
decisions.reason: Readable shows that a ritual washing is meant, not ordinary washing.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: He but answering said to them, Because of what also you break the commandment of the God because of the tradition of you?
pieces: He answered them, "And why do you go against God's commandment for the sake of your tradition?

L.3: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "Why do you also break the commandment of God because of your tradition?

R.3: Jesus answered, "And why do you break God's command so that you can keep your own rules?

decisions.choice: you also: Jesus turns their charge back on them
alternatives: you as well as my disciples
decisions.reason: They accused the disciples of breaking a tradition. Jesus asks why they themselves break a command of God, which is far more serious.

decisions.choice: your tradition: rules of human making, set against God's command
decisions.reason: In 15:2 it was "the tradition of the elders". Jesus now calls it "your tradition", their own, in contrast with what God commanded.

decisions.choice: Jesus answered
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:9
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 3-9 are one answer, so the quotation marks stay open to the end.

records.source: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·
records.gloss: The for God said, Honor the father and the mother, and, The [one] speaking evil of father or mother in death let him end;
pieces: For God said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and also, 'Anyone who reviles father or mother must be put to death.'

L.4: For God said, 'Honor [your] father and [your] mother,' and, 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must surely die.'

R.4: God said, 'Honor your father and your mother.' He also said, 'Anyone who says evil things against their father or mother must be put to death.'

decisions.choice: honor your father and your mother: Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 5:16
decisions.reason: The fifth commandment. Jesus calls it what God said, not only what Moses said.

decisions.choice: whoever speaks evil of father or mother: Exodus 21:17; Leviticus 20:9
decisions.reason: The law treated cursing a parent as a crime deserving death. "Let him end in death" copies a Hebrew way of speaking that stresses certainty.

decisions.choice: honor: respect, and also support and care for parents in old age
decisions.reason: Honoring parents included providing for them. This is the point of the example in 15:5-6.

decisions.choice: God said, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: God commanded, saying, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "God commanded, saying". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: reviles
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak evil of someone, to abuse with words.

records.source: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς, οὐ μὴ τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: You but say, Whoever shall say to the father or the mother, A gift whatever by me you might be profited, \v 6 not not he shall honor the father of him; and you made void the word of the God because of the tradition of you.
pieces: But you teach that if someone says to father or mother, 'Any support you could have received from me is set apart as a gift to God,'
then that person is excused from honoring {{gender:their|his}} father. So for the sake of your tradition you have cancelled God's word.

L.5: But you say, 'Whoever says to father or mother, "Whatever help you might have had from me [is] a gift [to God],"
L.6: {{gender:that person|he}} shall certainly not honor {{gender:their|his}} father.' And you have made void the word of God because of your tradition.

R.5: But you teach something else. You say people can tell their father or mother, 'I cannot help you. What I would have given you is now a gift for God.'
R.6: Then they do not have to honor their father anymore. So you make God's word mean nothing, just to keep your own rules.

decisions.choice: a gift: property vowed to God, so that it could not be used for the parents
decisions.reason: Mark 7:11 gives the Hebrew word for such an offering, Corban. Vows to God were binding (Numbers 30:2). A son could declare his goods vowed to God and so put them beyond his parents' reach, while he may still have kept the use of them himself.

decisions.choice: shall not honor his father: the result of their ruling, that such a person is freed from the duty
alternatives: Jesus's own comment: such a person will certainly not honor his father
decisions.reason: The words can be the last part of the teaching Jesus reports, saying the vow releases the son from supporting his father. They can also be Jesus's comment on what follows from it. Either way, the vow ends the son's care for his parents.

decisions.choice: the word of God, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the commandment of God, the reading of many later manuscripts
the law of God, in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "the word", others "the law", and many later ones "the commandment". All three point to the command of 15:4. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his father, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: his father or his mother, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "or his mother", to match 15:4 and 15:5. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|he}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The rule applies to a daughter as well as a son, so the inclusive forms are the default.

decisions.choice: I cannot help you; anymore
alternatives: a gift; he shall not honor
decisions.reason: Readable says what the vow meant for the parents.

decisions.choice: cancelled (B); make mean nothing (R)
decisions.reason: The verb was used for annulling a law or a contract.

records.source: ὑποκριταί, καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν περὶ ὑμῶν Ἠσαΐας λέγων·
records.gloss: Hypocrites, rightly prophesied concerning you Isaiah saying,
pieces: You are hypocrites, and Isaiah's prophecy about you was exactly right. He said:

L.7: Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied rightly about you, saying,

R.7: You hypocrites! Long ago Isaiah spoke God's message, and he described you exactly. He said,

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people whose religion is a performance
decisions.reason: As in 6:2. Their outward care for purity hides a heart far from God (15:8).

decisions.choice: prophesied about you: Isaiah's words to his own generation fit these leaders too
alternatives: Isaiah spoke only of people in Jesus's day
decisions.reason: Isaiah spoke to the people of Jerusalem in his own time. Jesus says the words describe his hearers just as well.

decisions.choice: spoke God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying is.

records.source: Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ·
records.gloss: The people this with the lips me honors, the but heart of them far away is from me;
pieces: 'With their lips this people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but their heart keeps far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.8: 'This people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with [their] lips, but their heart is far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};

R.8: 'These people honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their words, but their hearts are far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 29:13: God speaks of his people
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes in a form close to the Greek Old Testament. In Isaiah the Lord is the speaker, so "me" is God.

decisions.choice: this people honors me with their lips, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: this people draws near to me with their mouth and honors me with their lips, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "draws near to me with their mouth and", which is in the Greek of Isaiah 29:13. Early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where thoughts and choices begin
decisions.reason: As in 12:34. Honor in words means nothing when the heart, the person's real self, stays away from God.

decisions.choice: spans on "me" for God
decisions.reason: God speaks in Isaiah, so the pronouns for him take the deity_pronoun setting, as in 12:18.

decisions.choice: with their words
decisions.reason: Readable says what honoring with the lips means.

records.source: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: In vain but they worship me, teaching [as] teachings commandments of men.
pieces: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is empty, for the doctrines they teach are commands made by human beings.'"

L.9: and in vain they worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, teaching [as] teachings [the] commandments of {{gender:people|men}}.'"

R.9: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} means nothing. They teach rules that people made up, as if those rules came from God.'"

decisions.choice: in vain: to no purpose, empty
decisions.reason: Their worship achieves nothing, because God does not accept it.

decisions.choice: teaching as doctrines the commands of people: presenting human rules as God's teaching
alternatives: teaching both God's law and human rules
decisions.reason: The fault is that rules made by people are taught as if they had God's authority. That is what Jesus has shown in 15:3-6.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: as if those rules came from God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "teaching as doctrines" means here.

records.source: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀκούετε καὶ συνίετε·
records.gloss: And having called to [him] the crowd he said to them, Hear and understand;
pieces: Then Jesus called the crowd over to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Hear this, and understand it.

L.10: And calling the crowd to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Listen and understand:

R.10: Then Jesus called the crowd to come near. He said, "Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and understand what I say.

decisions.choice: calling the crowd: the teaching is for everyone, not only the leaders
alternatives: a private word to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from the Pharisees and scribes to the whole crowd. What makes a person unclean concerns everyone.

decisions.choice: understand: grasp the meaning, not only hear the words
decisions.reason: The same verb runs through the parables of chapter 13 (13:13-15, 19, 23). Hearing is not enough without understanding.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new part of the scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:11
alternatives: closing the quotation in this sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 10-11 are one saying.

records.heading: What makes a person unclean

records.source: οὐ τὸ εἰσερχόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦτο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
records.gloss: Not the entering into the mouth defiles the man, but the going out of the mouth this defiles the man.
pieces: A person is not made unclean by what goes into the mouth. What makes a person unclean is what comes out of it."

L.11: It is not what enters into the mouth [that] defiles the {{gender:person|man}}, but what comes out of the mouth, this defiles the {{gender:person|man}}."

R.11: What you put into your mouth does not make you unclean before God. It is what comes out of your mouth that makes you unclean."

decisions.choice: defiles: makes a person unclean, unfit to come before God
decisions.reason: The verb means to make common or impure. Purity decided whether a person could take part in worship (Leviticus 11-15).

decisions.choice: what comes out of the mouth: words, and the heart they come from
decisions.reason: Jesus explains in 15:18-19 that what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart.

decisions.choice: the saying answers the question of washed hands (15:20)
alternatives: a ruling that sets aside all the food laws
decisions.reason: Matthew applies the saying to eating with unwashed hands (15:20) and does not include Mark's comment that Jesus made all foods clean (Mark 7:19). How far the saying bears on the food laws themselves is debated.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, so the inclusive form is the default. The same applies in 15:18 and 15:20.

decisions.choice: before God
decisions.reason: Readable says in whose sight a person is unclean.

records.source: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οἶδας ὅτι οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον ἐσκανδαλίσθησαν;
records.gloss: Then having come the disciples say to him, Do you know that the Pharisees having heard the saying were offended?
pieces: Then the disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} aware that the Pharisees took offense at what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said?"

L.12: Then the disciples come and say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard the saying?"

R.12: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that the Pharisees were upset by what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said?"

decisions.choice: were offended: were shocked and angered, and so turned against him
decisions.reason: The verb pictures stumbling over something (11:6). The saying made them reject Jesus's teaching.

decisions.choice: the saying: the words of 15:11
decisions.reason: The disciples most likely mean the saying about what defiles. It struck at the purity rules the Pharisees kept with care.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: what you said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose saying it was.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ἐκριζωθήσεται.
records.gloss: He but answering said, Every plant which not planted the Father of me the heavenly will be uprooted.
pieces: He answered, "Any plant that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven did not plant will be torn out, roots and all.

L.13: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "Every plant which {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.

R.13: Jesus answered, "My Father in heaven will dig up every plant that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not plant.

decisions.choice: plant: the Pharisees and their teaching, which God did not plant
decisions.reason: Israel was pictured as God's planting (Isaiah 60:21; 61:3). Jesus says these leaders and their tradition do not come from God. Compare the weeds sown among the wheat (13:24-30).

decisions.choice: will be uprooted: God will uproot it, at the judgment
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the subject unsaid, but the Father who plants is the one who uproots. The next verse tells the disciples to leave them alone.

decisions.choice: My Father in heaven will dig up
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who acts, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:14
alternatives: closing the quotation in this sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 13-14 are one answer.

records.source: ἄφετε αὐτούς· τυφλοί εἰσιν ὁδηγοί τυφλῶν· τυφλὸς δὲ τυφλὸν ἐὰν ὁδηγῇ, ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον πεσοῦνται.
records.gloss: Leave them; blind they are guides of blind; blind and blind if guides, both into a pit will fall.
pieces: Pay no attention to them. They are blind, yet they guide others who are blind. When one blind person guides another, the two of them end up in a ditch."

L.14: Leave them; they are blind guides of [the] blind. And if a blind [person] guides a blind [person], both will fall into a pit."

R.14: Do not worry about them. They are like blind people leading other blind people. If a blind person leads another blind person, they will both fall into a hole."

decisions.choice: leave them: let them be; do not be troubled about them
decisions.reason: The verb has a range of meanings. Here Jesus tells the disciples not to worry about the Pharisees' offense.

decisions.choice: blind guides: teachers who cannot see God's will and lead others astray
alternatives: people who are blind in body
decisions.reason: Teachers of the law saw themselves as guides of the blind (Romans 2:19). Jesus says they cannot see themselves (23:16, 24).

decisions.choice: blind guides of the blind, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: they are blind guides, in some early manuscripts
the same words in a different order, in others
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here. Some early ones lack "of the blind", and others order the words differently. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: ditch
decisions.reason: The word means a hole or ditch in the ground. Balanced uses the word most natural for a fall on a road.

records.source: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Φράσον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολήν ταύτην.
records.gloss: Answering and the Peter said to him, Explain to us the parable this.
pieces: Peter spoke up: "Tell us what this parable means."

L.15: And Peter answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Explain this parable to us."

R.15: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Explain to us what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} meant by this saying."

decisions.choice: parable: a saying in picture language, a riddle
decisions.reason: The word covers short sayings as well as stories. Peter means the saying of 15:11, and perhaps of 15:13-14 too.

decisions.choice: answered: spoke up in response to what had been said
decisions.reason: No question was asked. As often, the word introduces a reply to the situation. Peter speaks for the disciples (15:16 answers them all).

decisions.choice: this saying
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word, since there is no story here.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἀκμὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε;
records.gloss: He and said, Still also you without understanding are?
pieces: He said, "Are even you still so slow to understand?

L.16: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Are you also still without understanding?

R.16: Jesus said, "Even now, do you still not understand, just like the others?

decisions.choice: you also: even the disciples, like the crowd and the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Jesus expected his disciples to understand what outsiders did not (13:11, 16).

decisions.choice: still: even now, after all they have heard
decisions.reason: The word stresses how long they have been with him.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:20
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 16-20 are one answer.

records.source: οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν χωρεῖ καὶ εἰς ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκβάλλεται;
records.gloss: Not do you understand that everything entering into the mouth into the stomach goes and into a latrine is cast out?
pieces: Can you not see that everything taken in by the mouth goes down into the stomach and is then passed out into the latrine?

L.17: Do you not understand that everything that enters into the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled into [the] latrine?

R.17: You know that the food you eat goes into your stomach and then passes out of your body.

decisions.choice: latrine: the place where waste is passed
decisions.reason: The word names a toilet or drain. Food passes through the body and is gone.

decisions.choice: do you not understand: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: Jesus asks them to see what is plain: food never reaches the heart.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question assumes.

records.source: τὰ δὲ ἐκπορευόμενα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχεται, κἀκεῖνα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
records.gloss: The things but going out of the mouth out of the heart come out, and those defile the man.
pieces: But what comes out of the mouth has its source in the heart, and that is what makes a person unclean.

L.18: But the things coming out of the mouth come out of the heart, and those defile the {{gender:person|man}}.

R.18: But what comes out of your mouth comes from your heart. Those things make you unclean.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where thoughts and choices begin
decisions.reason: As in 15:8. What a person says and does comes from what is within (12:34).

decisions.choice: uncleanness begins inside a person
alternatives: uncleanness is only a matter of the body
decisions.reason: Jesus moves the question from the hands and the stomach to the heart.

records.source: ἐκ γὰρ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχονται διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί, φόνοι, μοιχεῖαι, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, ψευδομαρτυρίαι, βλασφημίαι.
records.gloss: Out of for the heart come out thoughts evil, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, slanders.
pieces: It is from the heart that evil schemes come, and murder, adultery and other sexual sin, theft, false witness and abusive speech.

L.19: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, slanders.

R.19: The heart is where evil thoughts come from. Murder, adultery, other sexual sins, stealing, lying in court, and saying hurtful things about others all come from there too.

decisions.choice: murder, adultery, theft, false witness: the order of the sixth to ninth commandments
decisions.reason: The list follows Exodus 20:13-16. Jesus has spoken of the fifth commandment in 15:4.

decisions.choice: evil thoughts: wicked plans and reasonings
decisions.reason: The word means reasonings or plans. They are named first, as the root of the deeds that follow.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual sin of every kind
decisions.reason: The word is broad and covers sexual sin besides adultery.

decisions.choice: slanders: abusive speech against others, or against God
decisions.reason: The word can mean blasphemy against God or slander against people. Next to false witness, harm to others is in view, though both may be meant.

decisions.choice: evil schemes (B); lying in court (R); abusive speech (B), saying hurtful things about others (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe each wrong in plain words.

records.source: ταῦτά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον, τὸ δὲ ἀνίπτοις χερσὶν φαγεῖν οὐ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
records.gloss: These are the things defiling the man, the but with unwashed hands to eat not defiles the man.
pieces: These are what make a person unclean. Eating without washing one's hands does not make anyone unclean."

L.20: These are the things that defile the {{gender:person|man}}; but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile the {{gender:person|man}}."

R.20: These are the things that make a person unclean. But if you eat without washing your hands in the special way, that does not make you unclean."

decisions.choice: eating with unwashed hands: the answer to the question of 15:2
decisions.reason: The chapter returns to where it began. The tradition of washing does not decide whether a person is clean before God.

decisions.choice: in the special way
decisions.reason: As in 15:2, Readable shows that a ritual washing is meant.

records.source: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος.
records.gloss: And having gone out from there the Jesus withdrew into the districts of Tyre and Sidon.
pieces: Jesus left that place and went away to the region around Tyre and Sidon.

L.21: And going out from there, Jesus withdrew into the districts of Tyre and Sidon.

R.21: Jesus left that place and went to the area near the cities of Tyre and Sidon.

decisions.choice: Tyre and Sidon: Gentile cities on the coast north of Galilee
decisions.reason: The two cities were in Phoenicia. Jesus named them in 11:21-22 as Gentile towns that would have repented.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away, as after opposition before
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the verb when Jesus moves away after conflict (12:15; 14:13).

decisions.choice: into the districts: to the area of Tyre and Sidon, perhaps only near the border
decisions.reason: The woman "came out from those regions" (15:22), which may mean that Jesus stayed near the border. Matthew does not say exactly where he was.

decisions.choice: the cities of
decisions.reason: Readable says that these are cities.

records.heading: A Canaanite mother's faith

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ Χαναναία ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων ἐκείνων ἐξελθοῦσα ἔκραζεν λέγουσα· Ἐλέησόν με, κύριε υἱὸς Δαυίδ· ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται.
records.gloss: And behold, a woman Canaanite from the regions those having come out was crying out saying, Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; the daughter of me badly is demon-possessed.
pieces: A Canaanite woman who lived in that region came out and kept calling out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! A demon has my daughter in its grip, and she suffers terribly."

L.22: And look, a Canaanite woman from those regions came out and was crying out, saying, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is severely demon-possessed."

R.22: A woman from that area came to Jesus. She was a Canaanite, not a Jew. She kept shouting, "Lord, Son of David, please have pity on me! My daughter has a demon, and it is hurting her terribly."

decisions.choice: Canaanite: a Gentile of that region, called by the ancient name of Israel's neighbors
alternatives: a descendant of the Canaanites only
decisions.reason: The Canaanites were the peoples of the land before Israel. Mark 7:26 calls her a Syrophoenician by birth. Matthew's older name sets her among Israel's ancient neighbors.

decisions.choice: Son of David: the title of the promised king
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, the title names Jesus as the Messiah. A Gentile woman uses Israel's own title for him.

decisions.choice: Lord: a respectful address, and in Matthew more than that
decisions.reason: As in 8:2, those who come in faith call Jesus "Lord". She uses the word three times (15:22, 25, 27).

decisions.choice: was crying out: she kept calling
decisions.reason: The tense shows she went on calling, as the disciples complain in 15:23.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: not a Jew
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name meant for the story.

records.source: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῇ λόγον.
records.gloss: He but not answered her a word.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave her no answer, not even a word.

L.23: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not answer her a word.

R.23: But Jesus did not say anything to her.

decisions.choice: did not answer her a word: complete silence
decisions.reason: Matthew says that Jesus was silent but not why. His words in 15:24 explain the limit he felt bound by.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἠρώτουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἀπόλυσον αὐτήν, ὅτι κράζει ὄπισθεν ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: And having come the disciples of him were urging him saying, Send away her, because she cries out after us.
pieces: His disciples came and kept pressing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Send her away, because she keeps shouting behind us."

L.23: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came and were urging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us."

R.23: His followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Send her away! She keeps following us and shouting."

decisions.choice: send her away: get rid of her, perhaps by giving her what she asks
decisions.reason: The verb means to release or dismiss. The disciples may want her sent off with nothing, or want Jesus to grant her request so she will go. Jesus's answer in 15:24 fits either.

decisions.choice: were urging: they kept on asking
decisions.reason: The tense shows repeated asking.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀπεστάλην εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: He but answering said, Not I was sent except to the sheep the being lost of house of Israel.
pieces: He answered, "I was sent only to the lost sheep, the people of Israel."

L.24: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "I was not sent except to the lost sheep of [the] house of Israel."

R.24: Jesus answered, "God sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} only to the people of Israel. They are like sheep that are lost."

decisions.choice: the lost sheep of the house of Israel: the words of 10:6
alternatives: only the lost ones within Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus sent the twelve to the same people (10:6). The whole nation is the lost flock (9:36). The wording is kept the same as in 10:6 at each level.

decisions.choice: I was sent: sent by God
alternatives: I came of my own accord
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the sender unnamed, and the sender is God (10:40).

decisions.choice: a limit for Jesus's earthly mission, not for all time
alternatives: a rule that God cares only for Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus comes first to Israel. After his resurrection he sends his disciples to all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: God sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names the sender.

records.source: ἡ δὲ ἐλθοῦσα προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγουσα· Κύριε, βοήθει μοι.
records.gloss: She but having come was kneeling to him saying, Lord, help me.
pieces: But she came and bowed low before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Lord," she said, "help me!"

L.25: But she came and knelt before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, help me."

R.25: Then the woman came and bowed down in front of Jesus. She said, "Lord, help me!"

decisions.choice: knelt before him: bowed low in honor and appeal
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 2:11, 8:2 and 9:18. Here it is the bow of one asking a great favor, though Matthew's readers hear more in it (14:33).

decisions.choice: help me: her plea for her daughter
decisions.reason: She asks help for herself, since her daughter's suffering is hers too.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔστιν καλὸν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ βαλεῖν τοῖς κυναρίοις.
records.gloss: He but answering said, Not it is good to take the bread of the children and to throw [it] to the little dogs.
pieces: He replied, "It is not good to take bread away from the children and toss it to the little dogs."

L.26: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw [it] to the little dogs."

R.26: Jesus answered, "It is not right to take the children's food and throw it to the pet dogs."

decisions.choice: little dogs: house dogs kept indoors
alternatives: dogs in general, with no softening
decisions.reason: The word is a small form of the word for dog and fits dogs under a family table (15:27). Small forms often lost their force in the Greek of this time, so the word may simply mean dogs. And "dogs" was a name some Jews used for Gentiles, so the saying is still a hard one.

decisions.choice: the children: Israel; the dogs: the Gentiles
alternatives: a general proverb with no reference
decisions.reason: The saying applies 15:24 in a picture. The children of the household are fed first.

decisions.choice: it is not right: it is not fitting, like a household rule
decisions.reason: The word speaks of what is proper.

decisions.choice: food; pet dogs
decisions.reason: Readable shows that these are dogs living in the house, as in Mark 7:27, and says that bread here means food.

records.source: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, κύριε, καὶ γὰρ τὰ κυνάρια ἐσθίει ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τῶν κυρίων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: She but said, Yes, Lord, even for the little dogs eat from the crumbs the falling from the table of the masters of them.
pieces: She said, "That is true, Lord. Still, the little dogs eat some of the crumbs that drop from the table where their masters eat."

L.27: But she said, "Yes, Lord, for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."

R.27: She said, "Yes, Lord. But even the pet dogs get to eat the crumbs that fall from the table where their owners eat."

decisions.choice: yes ... for even: she accepts his picture and finds room in it for herself
decisions.reason: She agrees that the children come first. The dogs, she says, are fed in the same house at the same meal, from what falls.

decisions.choice: masters: the owners of the house, the same word as "Lord"
decisions.reason: She calls Jesus Lord and speaks of the dogs' masters with the same word. The point is that the dogs belong to the household.

decisions.choice: Still (B); But even (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show how her reply turns his saying.

decisions.choice: owners
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word for the people a dog belongs to.

records.source: τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Ὦ γύναι, μεγάλη σου ἡ πίστις· γενηθήτω σοι ὡς θέλεις.
records.gloss: Then answering the Jesus said to her, O woman, great of you the faith; let it be to you as you wish.
pieces: Then Jesus told her, "Woman, your faith is great. May it be done for you as you wish."

L.28: Then Jesus answered and said to her, "O woman, great [is] your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish."

R.28: Then Jesus answered her, "Woman, your faith is very great! What you asked for will happen."

decisions.choice: faith: her trust in Jesus's power and mercy
alternatives: her belief in a set of teachings
decisions.reason: She kept asking, even when refused. Matthew praises the faith of a Gentile, as with the centurion (8:10), while the disciples have "little faith" (14:31).

decisions.choice: O woman: a strong, respectful address
decisions.reason: The added word gives feeling to the address. "Woman" was a polite way to speak to a woman.

decisions.choice: let it be done: Jesus's word grants the healing
decisions.reason: As in 8:13, Jesus heals at a distance by his word.

records.source: καὶ ἰάθη ἡ θυγάτηρ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
records.gloss: And was healed the daughter of her from the hour that.
pieces: And from that moment her daughter was well.

L.28: And her daughter was healed from that hour.

R.28: Her daughter was healed at that very moment.

decisions.choice: from that hour: at the moment Jesus spoke
decisions.reason: As in 8:13 and 9:22. The healing came at once, without Jesus going to the girl.

records.source: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἀναβὰς εἰς τὸ ὄρος ἐκάθητο ἐκεῖ.
records.gloss: And having moved on from there the Jesus came beside the sea of the Galilee, and having gone up into the mountain he was sitting there.
pieces: From there Jesus moved on and came along the shore of the Sea of Galilee. He went up onto the mountain and sat down there.

L.29: And moving on from there, Jesus came beside the Sea of Galilee, and going up onto the mountain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down there.

R.29: Jesus went on from there and walked along the shore of Lake Galilee. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on a hill and sat down.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Galilee: the large freshwater lake
decisions.reason: As in 4:18. The lake is called a sea.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hills by the lake, not named
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "the mountain", as in 5:1 and 14:23.

decisions.choice: sat down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: As in 5:1, Jewish teachers sat to teach. Here the crowds come to him there.

decisions.choice: Lake Galilee
decisions.reason: As in 4:18, Readable says it is a lake.

records.heading: Healing on the mountain by the lake

records.source: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἔχοντες μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν κωφούς, τυφλούς, χωλούς, κυλλούς, καὶ ἑτέρους πολλούς, καὶ ἔρριψαν αὐτοὺς παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς·
records.gloss: And came to him crowds great having with themselves mute, blind, lame, crippled, and others many, and they threw them at the feet of him, and he healed them;
pieces: Large crowds came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, bringing people who could not speak, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others. They laid them down at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

L.30: And great crowds came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having with them [the] mute, blind, lame, crippled, and many others, and they laid them at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

R.30: Large crowds of people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They brought people who could not talk, people who were blind, people who could not walk, people whose arms or legs were damaged, and many others. They put them down in front of Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

decisions.choice: mute: unable to speak
decisions.reason: The word can mean deaf or mute (11:5). In 15:31 they are seen speaking, so the mute are meant.

decisions.choice: crippled: with a hand or limb deformed or maimed
decisions.reason: The word is different from "lame" and describes a twisted or damaged limb.

decisions.choice: laid them: put them down in haste
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or cast. It shows how eager the crowds were, not that the sick were handled roughly.

decisions.choice: mute, blind, lame, crippled, the order of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the same four in other orders
decisions.reason: Manuscripts give the list in several orders. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: ὥστε τὸν ὄχλον θαυμάσαι βλέποντας κωφοὺς λαλοῦντας κυλλοὺς ὑγιεῖς καὶ χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας καὶ τυφλοὺς βλέποντας· καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: So that the crowd marveled seeing mute speaking, crippled whole, and lame walking, and blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.
pieces: The crowd was amazed to see the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking and the blind able to see. And they glorified the God of Israel.

L.31: So the crowd marveled, seeing [the] mute speaking, [the] crippled whole, and [the] lame walking, and [the] blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

R.31: The people were amazed. Those who could not talk were talking. People whose arms or legs were damaged were well again. People who could not walk were walking, and blind people could see. And the crowd gave glory to the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: the God of Israel: perhaps praise from Gentiles, perhaps a Jewish form of praise
alternatives: a phrase with no special meaning here
decisions.reason: The words may mean that the crowd was largely Gentile, praising Israel's God; Mark 7:31 places a healing at this time in the Ten Towns. But the phrase is also a Jewish form of praise (Psalm 41:13; Luke 1:68), and Matthew does not say who the crowd were.

decisions.choice: the mute speak, the lame walk, the blind see: Isaiah 35:5-6
alternatives: a simple report with no background
decisions.reason: As in 11:5, these are the signs Isaiah promised for the time when God comes to save.

decisions.choice: the crippled whole, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: no mention of the crippled, in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "the crippled whole". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: glorified: praised God and gave him honor
decisions.reason: As in 9:8, the crowd gives God the honor for what he has done.

decisions.choice: gave glory to
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term in a simpler phrase, as in 9:8.

records.source: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν· καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτοὺς νήστεις οὐ θέλω, μήποτε ἐκλυθῶσιν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
records.gloss: The and Jesus having called to [him] the disciples of him said, I have compassion on the crowd, because already days three they remain with me and not they have anything they may eat; and to send away them hungry not I am willing, lest they faint on the way.
pieces: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples together and said, "I feel deep pity for the crowd. For three days now they have stayed with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they have nothing left to eat. If I send them off without food, they may give out on the way, and I am not willing to do that."

L.32: And Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and said, "I have compassion on the crowd, because already for three days they remain with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they do not have anything to eat; and I am not willing to send them away hungry, lest they faint on the way."

R.32: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "I feel sorry for these people. They have been here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for three days, and now they have nothing to eat. If I send them home hungry, they may become weak and faint on the road. I do not want that."

decisions.choice: have compassion: be moved deep within with pity
decisions.reason: As in 9:36 and 14:14. The verb comes from the word for the inner parts, thought of as the seat of feeling.

decisions.choice: already three days: they have stayed so long that their food is gone
decisions.reason: The point is how long they have stayed with Jesus in a place far from towns.

decisions.choice: faint: give out from hunger and weakness
decisions.reason: The verb means to become weak or collapse.

decisions.choice: feel deep pity
decisions.reason: As in 9:36.

decisions.choice: the condition first, then Jesus's refusal
alternatives: I am not willing to send them away hungry, lest they faint
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the danger first and ends on Jesus's resolve.

records.heading: Bread for four thousand

records.source: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Πόθεν ἡμῖν ἐν ἐρημίᾳ ἄρτοι τοσοῦτοι ὥστε χορτάσαι ὄχλον τοσοῦτον;
records.gloss: And say to him the disciples, From where to us in a desolate place loaves so many as to satisfy a crowd so great?
pieces: The disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Here in this lonely place, where could we find enough bread to feed such a crowd?"

L.33: And the disciples say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where [are we to get] so many loaves in a desolate place to satisfy so great a crowd?"

R.33: His followers answered, "We are far away from any town. Where can we get enough bread to feed all these people?"

decisions.choice: a desolate place: open country, far from towns
decisions.reason: As in 14:15, the word means land with few people, not a desert of sand.

decisions.choice: the disciples' question after the feeding of 14:13-21
alternatives: a request that Jesus feed them again
decisions.reason: Matthew does not explain why they ask this after the first feeding. In 16:9-10 Jesus reminds them of both feedings.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: We are far away from any town
decisions.reason: Readable says what the place was like.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πόσους ἄρτους ἔχετε;
records.gloss: And says to them the Jesus, How many loaves have you?
pieces: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves have you got?"

L.34: And Jesus says to them, "How many loaves do you have?"

R.34: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves of bread do you have?"

decisions.choice: loaves: small flat loaves of bread
decisions.reason: A loaf was a small round bread, enough for one person's meal.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά, καὶ ὀλίγα ἰχθύδια.
records.gloss: They and said, Seven, and a few small fish.
pieces: "Seven," they said, "and a few little fish."

L.34: And they said, "Seven, and a few small fish."

R.34: They said, "Seven loaves, and a few small fish."

decisions.choice: small fish: little fish, probably dried or salted
decisions.reason: The word is a small form of the word for fish. Fish from the lake were often dried or salted and eaten with bread.

records.source: καὶ παραγγείλας τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἔλαβεν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς ἰχθύας καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.
records.gloss: And having directed the crowd to sit down on the ground \v 36 he took the seven loaves and the fish and having given thanks he broke and was giving to the disciples, the and disciples to the crowds.
pieces: He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and broke them. He kept handing them to the disciples, and the disciples handed them to the people.

L.35: And having directed the crowd to sit down on the ground,
L.36: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the seven loaves and the fish, and having given thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [them] and was giving [them] to the disciples, and the disciples [gave them] to the crowds.

R.35: Jesus told the people to sit down on the ground.
R.36: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the seven loaves and the fish and thanked God for them. He broke them into pieces and kept giving them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, and the followers gave them to the people.

decisions.choice: took, gave thanks, broke, gave: the actions of the first feeding and the Last Supper
decisions.reason: The same series comes at the first feeding (14:19) and at the Last Supper, where the verb for giving thanks is used of the cup (26:26-27).

decisions.choice: gave thanks: thanked God, as at the start of a Jewish meal
decisions.reason: At meals a Jew gave thanks to God for the food. At 14:19 Matthew says "blessed"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: was giving: he kept handing out the food
decisions.reason: The tense describes repeated action as the bread kept coming.

decisions.choice: thanked God for them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, to whom the thanks were given.

records.source: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων ἦραν ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας πλήρεις.
records.gloss: And ate all and were satisfied, and the remaining of the broken pieces they took up seven large baskets full.
pieces: Everyone ate until they were full. Then they gathered up the leftover pieces, and these filled seven large baskets.

L.37: And they all ate and were satisfied, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven large baskets full.

R.37: All the people ate as much as they wanted. Then they picked up the pieces of food that were left. They filled seven big baskets.

decisions.choice: large baskets: big woven baskets or hampers
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the basket of 14:20. It names a larger basket, big enough to let a man down over a wall (Acts 9:25). Jesus keeps the two words apart in 16:9-10.

decisions.choice: were satisfied: were fed until full
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 14:20 and 15:33.

decisions.choice: large baskets (L, B); big baskets (R)
decisions.reason: The size is part of the meaning of the word. Every level marks it so that readers can tell these baskets from those of 14:20, as in Mark 8:8.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν τετρακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.
records.gloss: Those and eating were four thousand men apart from women and children.
pieces: Those who ate numbered 4,000 men, and there were women and children besides.

L.38: And those who ate were 4,000 men, apart from women and children.

R.38: There were 4,000 men who ate, and there were also women and children.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word means men, not people in general, and Matthew adds that women and children were also there, as in 14:21. Mark 8:9 simply counts about 4,000.

decisions.choice: counting the men: a common way of counting a crowd
decisions.reason: Crowds were often counted by the men. Matthew makes clear that the whole crowd was larger.

decisions.choice: men, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Here the word means males, as the mention of women and children shows, so it takes no setting.

records.source: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἐνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Μαγαδάν.
records.gloss: And having sent away the crowds he got into the boat, and came into the region of Magadan.
pieces: After sending the crowds away, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.

L.39: And sending away the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat and came into the region of Magadan.

R.39: Then Jesus sent the people home. He got into the boat and went to the area of Magadan.

decisions.choice: Magadan, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Magdala, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read Magdala, the known town on the west shore of the lake, the home of Mary Magdalene. Scribes probably replaced an unknown name with a known one. Mark 8:10 has Dalmanutha. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Magadan: a place by the lake not known from any other source
decisions.reason: Where Magadan lay is not known. Pharisees and Sadducees meet Jesus there next (16:1), which suggests Jewish territory on the west side of the lake.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.
